facts.content: Patient reports a worsening, widespread itchy rash for the past few days.
facts.source_text: CC: Worsening, widespread itchy rash “past few days”

facts.content: Patient has sore, red, very dry eczema on chest, hands, and arms, especially in antecubital fossae.
facts.source_text: HPI: Sore, red, very dry eczema on chest, hands/arms, esp. antecubital fossae

facts.content: Eczema has cracked areas but no weeping or lichenification.
facts.source_text: cracked areas, no weeping, no lichenification

facts.content: There is no fever or arthralgia associated with the eczema.
Patient has a history of eczema.
Patient has a history of asthma.
Patient uses Diprobase emollient.
Patient uses Dermol wash.
Patient uses over-the-counter hydrocortisone 1% cream as needed.
Patient uses salbutamol (blue) inhaler as needed.
Patient has no known drug allergies.
Patient's mother has a history of migraines.
Patient's mother has a history of hypothyroidism.
There is an extensive flare of atopic dermatitis with symptomatic itch but no infection signs.
facts.source_text: 1. Atopic dermatitis flare – extensive; symptomatic itch, no infection signs

facts.content: Asthma is intermittent and stable.
Continue use of emollients (Diprobase, Dermol) liberally.
Apply a thin layer of Betnovate (betamethasone valerate) twice daily to affected skin for two weeks.
facts.source_text: Betnovate (betamethasone valerate) thin layer BID to affected skin × 2 wks

facts.content: Take Fexofenadine orally for pruritus.
Continue as-needed use of salbutamol inhaler.
Prescription sent to Boots pharmacy.
Patient advised to return sooner if worsening or adverse reaction occurs; otherwise, routine review in two weeks.
